transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-30
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Jules Perez (Orchid Head of Search), Anika Rao (ML Eng), Tom Whitaker (CTO)

Summary (auto): quick hosted API demo focusing on embeddings + rerank. Walked through Console, Optimize suggestions, touched on security and pilot plan.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick intro: I'm Maya, account lead. With me is Diego, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:11] Jules (Orchid): Doing good, thanks. Excited to see the embeddings/ rerank flow — we've been evaluating options for a while.
[00:18] Diego (Redwood SE): Great. We'll run through a short demo of the hosted embeddings endpoint, the reranker endpoint, and then show the Console + Optimize recs we generate from a sample workload. We'll try to keep it practical.
[00:29] Tom (Orchid CTO): Sounds good. high level: our current infra is open-source vector store + custom BM25 + in-house reranker. We're looking for lowering tail latency and unit cost.
[00:40] Diego: perfect. quick question: do you run short queries mostly, like titles and one-liners, or longer user queries?
[00:47] Anika: Mostly short. ~60% title queries, 30% paragraph queries, some multi-turn chat. Sequence lengths are generally under 128 tokens.
[00:57] [01:02] Maya: cool. that aligns well with the hosted profiles we recommend. We'll demo the embeddings endpoint first — it's a typical REST call, returns a fixed-dim vector.
[01:12] Diego: (screen share) here's the Console. Top-left: model catalog. For embedded workloads we often recommend our optimized open-models — they have lower latency/ cost profiles in the catalog. Note: some model names might show as Redwood-verified, others as 'community'.
[01:27] Jules: can you point out where we pick quantized vs full models?
[01:32] Diego: Yep — model variant dropdown. For inference we expose quantization tiers (8-bit, 4-bit float approximations) — the Console suggests a default based on your traffic profile. Optimize will propose a quantization setting for cost targets.
[01:45] [02:03] Diego: now the embeddings API call: POST /v1/embeddings with text payload. We'll demo with a small data set. Request returns vector and token meta. Watch the latency header.
[02:14] (demo run)
[02:22] Anika: latency looks sub-10ms for the smaller inputs, is that typical?
[02:26] Diego: For hosted profiled models and short sequences yes, median is often 8-20ms. tail depends on burst and batch config.
[02:35] [03:01] Maya: quick aside about cost: we report per-embedding unit and also token-based for generation endpoints. For embeddings you get per-vector pricing, and Optimize can estimate monthly spend given QPS and average doc size. We can run a cost simulation for your 10k queries sample.
[03:19] Tom: curious how reranking works — do you do a separate rerank endpoint or is it combined?
[03:25] Diego: We offer a dedicated reranker endpoint that takes query + candidate ids (or candidate texts) and returns a scoring + explanation. It's optimized to run smaller models with cross-encoders or to call a re-rank variant that uses a lightweight cross-attention path.
[03:39] Jules: So flow would be: embeddings vector search on your vector store, top-k candidates, then pass candidates + query to Redwood reranker for final ranking?
[03:48] Diego: Exactly. That lets you keep your vector store (we support standard vectors) and only pay rerank cost for top-k. We also have an option to host hybrid strategy where Redwood stores embeddings and handles retrieval + rerank in one route — saves a network hop but has tradeoffs.
[04:02] [04:20] Anika: in our case we might keep vectors in our cluster for data locality and call the reranker. Any friction with id passing? Authentication?
[04:29] Maya: we support API keys, and for Private/Dedicated we support VPC peering or private endpoints. Hosted has TLS + token auth; we can push SSO/SAML integration for enterprise account mapping.
[04:41] Tom: KMS? we need to prove keys never leave our control for certain buckets.
[04:46] Diego: We integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments; for hosted we offer envelope encryption and can do bring-your-own-key for enterprise tiers. We'll include the KMS notes in the security pack.
[04:58] [05:30] Diego: back to demo — showing reranker. POST /v1/rerank with query + candidates. Response shows score and a short explanation field (token-level importance is sometimes noisy, it's best-effort).
[05:42] (demo run with a news search example)
[05:54] Jules: the explanation field seems a bit sparse— can we export model logits or more debugging info?
[06:01] Diego: We surface per-candidate confidence and a lightweight token alignment. For deeper debugging we offer tracing and raw logits in Dedicated or Private with strict controls; hosted doesn't dump raw logits by default for risk reasons but we can enable richer traces for pilots.
[06:18] [06:45] Maya: wanted to show Console observability: per-route latency percentile, token breakdown, and cost. For example this route is embeddings-prod: you'll see token counts, med/95/99 latency, and a breakdown by model variant.
[06:58] Anika: can we set alerts on regression for NDCG or similar?
[07:05] Diego: Yes — Optimize can take your eval sets; we track quality metrics on each model rollout and can alert on regressions. Many customers wire that into PagerDuty or Slack.
[07:18] [07:50] Tom: about batching — what's Redwood's approach for hosted? we don't want higher p99 due to batching.
[07:58] Diego: We do continuous batching with latency SLOs: small automatic batches for throughput, and we let you configure target latency windows. Optimize recommends batch sizes based on your qps distribution. For strict P99 constraints we can recommend smaller batch windows or the Dedicated profile.
[08:15] [08:40] Jules: how about prefix caching / KV cache for multi-turn chat?
[08:46] Diego: We offer prefix caching for repeated prefixes and managed KV cache for decoder states. For retrieval rerank flows it's less relevant, but for chat or multi-step ranking it's useful to avoid recomputing embeddings for the same doc content.
[08:58] [09:20] (brief pause to share a customer dataset link)
[09:27] Anika: sharing our 10k query sample now (link pasted in chat).
[09:34] Maya: perfect — we'll use that for the bench. Diego will send the harness.
[09:40] [10:05] Diego: switching to Optimize tab — this is where we recommend quantization, cache policies, and a batching profile. Example: for your short queries we'll likely recommend 8-bit quantization + small batch windows; that'll reduce per-embedding cost by ~30% in our simulations.
[10:20] Jules: are there known tradeoffs on relevance when quantizing? any quality delta?
[10:25] Diego: Usually minimal on embeddings for 8-bit; 4-bit can introduce subtle shifts, so Optimize will surface a delta metric (we run evals on your prompt/queries). We strongly recommend A/Bing test the quantized variant on your eval set first.
[10:38] [11:02] Tom: can you run the rerank on our historical queries and produce an expected NDCG delta?
[11:09] Diego: yes — part of the pilot we propose: ingest sample queries + ground-truth labels and run both current stack and Redwood baseline to estimate NDCG/precision@k and latency. We'll provide a short report.
[11:22] [11:45] Anika: what about throughput limits on hosted? our peak QPS hits bursts during sales events.
[11:52] Maya: hosted has tiered rate limits and burst protection; Dedicated is recommended for predictable high throughput and reserved capacity. We can provision autoscale policies for Dedicated including burst options.
[12:06] Jules: how do you handle falling back if capacity is constrained? we need graceful degradation.
[12:12] Diego: Smart routing can fall back to a cheaper model variant or region; you can set fallback policies in the Console per-route. It can also degrade to a cheaper approximate rerank or a heuristic.
[12:26] [12:50] Tom: security questions: SOC2 Type II, penetration testing, SSO.
[12:56] Maya: we are SOC2 Type II and will include the cert in the security pack. Pen tests are done annually; for large customers we can include third-party audit reports. SSO/SAML and SCIM for provisioning are supported.
[13:10] [13:35] Anika: data retention and query logs — we need to avoid storing PII.
[13:42] Diego: Hosted can be configured to redact or not log payloads. For PII-sensitive workloads we'd recommend Private or Dedicated with customer-managed retention. We'll include retention policy docs.
[13:55] [14:30] (short demo of a rerank latency histogram and per-token cost)
[14:45] Jules: the cost numbers in Console look promising. can you break down per-1M queries cost including rerank on top-k=10?
[14:54] Maya: We'll run a cost sim and include it in the follow-up pricing sheet. In rough numbers, embeddings per-call + rerank per-topk is additive; Optimize will show exact currency math.
[15:10] [15:40] Diego: small note about SDKs: we have official python and node SDKs with typed responses — examples in the repo. We'll send sample code for your stack.
[15:52] Anika: great. the sample code for batching will help us integrate quickly.
[15:58] [16:20] Tom: a deeper technical question: if we keep vectors in-house and only call reranker, do you need the full document text for rerank?
[16:28] Diego: You can pass candidate ids and we can fetch candidates if you want Redwood to do retrieval, or you can pass candidate texts inline. Passing texts avoids a second network call if you already have them. There's also a compressed payload option if docs are large.
[16:45] [17:05] Maya: let's talk pilot spec: 2-week bench where Redwood runs both hosted rerank and a dedicated rerank run, and we'll compare latency and NDCG. Diego will provide harness and we run a 2-hour live bench during a chosen window.
[17:20] Jules: timeline-wise we want to ship by end of Q4 if pilot looks good.
[17:27] Maya: understood. we'll aim for pilot in mid-Oct and decision by mid-Nov.
[17:33] [18:00] (customer asks about competitor differences)
[18:07] Anika: how is this different from Pinecone + in-house ranker?
[18:12] Diego: Pinecone is a vector store; Redwood is a full inference runtime + routing + re-rank. You get serving optimizations, automatic caching and the rerank endpoint optimized for cross-encoders which reduces engineering glue.
[18:27] [18:50] (small cross-talk about internal infra)
[18:55] Tom: cost modeling is key. can we get a spreadsheet template?
[19:01] Maya: yes will send a cost template — fill in QPS, average doc size, top-k. we'll simulate.
[19:10] [19:40] (Diego shows the Console rollout UI and canary features)
[19:53] Diego: rollout supports canary % and automatic rollback on metric regressions. You can tie it to evaluation sets and to token-level cost budgets.
[20:06] Jules: nice. that would help us iterate.
[20:14] [20:40] Anika: about logs again — if we enable tracing, where do logs land?
[20:46] Diego: For hosted, logs go to Redwoods managed logging with retention options; you can export to S3 or to your SIEM. For Private, logs can remain on-prem.
[20:59] [21:30] (discussion briefly wanders to multi-lingual embeddings)
[21:37] Diego: we support multi-lingual embeddings; Optimize will pick a model variant based on language mix.
[21:47] [22:10] Tom: what are typical p99 numbers customers see for rerank?
[22:16] Diego: depends on top-k and model; for top-10 cross-encoder on hosted it's often 60-300ms p99; gen-rerank hybrids can be lower. We'll bench with your dataset.
[22:29] [22:55] (customer asks about on-prem options for compliance)
[23:02] Maya: we offer Private deployments for air-gapped or VPC setups, with KMS integration and SOC2 support. It's typically an enterprise engagement.
[23:18] Anika: cost of Private seems high — is there a minimum term?
[23:24] Maya: yes typically annual licensing with a platform fee; we'll include ballpark numbers in the follow-up.
[23:34] [24:00] Diego: quick note — when we do the bench we instrument both model variants to capture latency percentiles, token counts and exact NDCG. This is part of the deliverable.
[24:12] (demo continues; Diego shows trace of a failing request)
[24:22] Diego: here you can see where a request hit a cold KV cache and spiked. We have cache warmup strategies.
[24:33] Jules: interesting — we've seen cold starts hurt during peak events.
[24:39] Diego: for Dedicated we can pin warm instances to reduce cold start impact.
[24:45] [25:10] (discussion of SLA and uptime)
[25:16] Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA and advanced support; hosted has generous uptime and we offer paid support add-on.
[25:30] [26:00] Anika: any limits on output size for rerank explanation?
[26:06] Diego: we cap explanation size on hosted but you can request extended debug for pilots.
[26:20] [26:50] (short Q&A; customers ask about edge-caching)
[26:57] Diego: Edge-caching is effective for static docs; for dynamic content we recommend TTL-based caches and incremental updates.
[27:08] [27:30] (wrap-up prep)
[27:36] Maya: quick recap: Redwood will send pilot SOW & pricing, Diego sends harness and sample SDK snippets, customer shares 10k queries, we schedule bench window. Anything else?
[27:53] Tom: include SOC2 + KMS details in the security pack.
[27:59] Maya: will do.
[28:10] [28:40] Jules: one last thing — can you show a snippet of the rerank request/response we can paste straight into our integration?
[28:47] Diego: (pastes sample curl) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"query":"who won 2024 world cup","candidates":[{"id":"d1","text":"Argentina beat..."},{"id":"d2","text":"France lost to..."}] }' Response: {"scores":[0.92,0.18],"explanations":["match tokens: argentina, world, cup","match tokens: france"]}
[29:08] Anika: that's helpful.
[29:13] [29:40] (final clarifying questions; small cross talk)
[29:50] Maya: we'll follow up with the sheet and the security pack. feel free to reply-all with any missing items.
[30:05] Tom: thanks everyone.
[30:10] (meeting ends — note: Fireflies truncated final 24 minutes of live Q&A due to manual stop)

Notes about transcript quality: automated transcription had a few mis-hearings (e.g., 'KV cache' transcribed sometimes as 'KV cash', 'quantization' as 'quantize Asian'). Speaker labels occasionally coalesced into 'Speaker 3' in parts.
